_meta.purpose: Non-improving code lane: blocking counts 1/1/2/1; halts at re-entry 4 with max 3 under BOTH the counting guard and the whole-lap rule — a trail that never gets strictly better still halts at the same re-entry. Lap 1 pins the severity floor (pattern-following pass:false severity low is non-blocking) and carries lap 1 code-confirm row (correctness upheld post-confirm).
_meta.excerpt_rule: Trail lines 52-99 in verbatim order: every code-cite-check row, every code-grade unit row, lap 1 code-confirm row, the four code-snapshot and four code-fix rows (round delimiters), all routing rows, and the halt row. Dropped within the range: the four code-demote stage rows.
_meta.channel_rule: Each stage row bakes its outcome channel in `channel` (derived from the workflow's outcome map so the replay needs no workflow introspection): code-cite-check->code-cite-check; code-grade/code-confirm->code-verdicts; code-snapshot->code-snapshot; code-fix->plans. code-demote publishes no channel and its rows are dropped.
_meta.trim_rule: Stage rows keep stageNumber/stage/channel plus the fold-read fields only: verdict rows (code-grade units + code-confirm) keep dimension/pass/severity/artifact and findings trimmed to the first finding {detail} (the anchor-nit clamp inside the blocking predicate reads findings; on this trail the clamp never decides a recorded count — every blocking verdict is pass:false severity medium, every waived one passes or sits at low/none); cite-check rows keep dimension/pass/severity; snapshot rows keep their prior fs handle; code-fix rows keep the plans fs handle + phase_count. Dropped: score/graded_at/feedback/kind/meta/ts, risk_rulings (the blocking predicate is risk-blind), verdict rows own artifacts array. Routing rows keep type/fromStage/decision verbatim. The halt row is normalized to the new kind {type:halt,stage,errMsg} with errMsg verbatim.
_meta.row_format: compact one-row-per-line JSON (each rows[] element on a single line)

findings.detail: Acceptance a7 / FRD FR2.2 enumerate floor-fail classes (missing file, out-of-range line, blank or divider line) that the plan keeps ADVISORY — verified against the live tree, every resolution finding in citations.ts is advisory today and Phase 1 explicitly preserves that tier, so only the new symbol class plus verifyPhaseFilesCoverage can produce the blocking floor fail that triggers the pre-panel fix route; the advisory/blocking rationale is documented in-plan (tier describe, zero-fabrications-audit precedent behind r8) but the narrowing relative to the FRD's class list is not explicitly flagged as a deviation the way r7 ratifies the FR3.1 fold-vs-emit change.

Phase 4's new built-ins/verdict-outcome.ts imports getSubagentUsageForStage from ../subagent-usage.js — the first production import from the built-ins cluster up to a parent-level rpiv-core module (every existing built-ins import is intra-cluster or package-level; verified by import sweep). Defensible rather than a violation: the factory must serve ship's twin outcome in built-ins/grade-panel.ts without creating a monolith cycle, subagent-usage.ts itself imports only ./lane-usage.js so the new edge is acyclic, and the plan documents the seam rationale as risk r3 — but the rpiv-core architecture doc's module map does not yet describe this edge shape, so the guidance file will need a one-line update when the module lands.

Phase 6's two new Python files are tab-indented throughout the emitted code blocks (844 tab-indented lines, zero space-indented), but the dominant local precedent is 4-space: all four existing sibling scripts in the same directory (baseline.py, replay.py, rerun-policies.py, simulate.py) use 4-space indentation exclusively, and no other Python exists in the repo. The plan names no reason for the divergence. Cosmetic in effect (consistently tabbed Python runs; the tree is gitignored research tooling; no Phase 6 AV checks style) but a genuine miss against the pass bar's aligns-or-justifies rule.

Phase 1 grade-panel.ts Edit 4 ships a comment asserting every route that reaches a panel leaves blocking floor findings repaired so the grader never receives an unrepaired blocking finding — false in the shape the plan's own routing and tests pin: on a first pass (or any round with a pending dimension or risk) over a red floor, planGatePasses and planFloorOnlyRed are both false and the edge routes to plan-grade, where citeCheckFlag threads the blocking floor verdict to the correctness unit as leads. The copied-verbatim comment misstates behavior and papers over the letter of goal FR2.2 (routes to fix before the panel spawns ... The judge never sees a resolution failure) in that shape.

Upheld from prior round: Phase 1 grade-panel.ts Edit 4 ships a doc comment asserting every route that reaches a panel leaves blocking floor findings repaired so the grader never receives an unrepaired blocking finding — false in the plan's own pinned shapes: on a first pass or any round with a pending dimension or failed risk over a red floor, qualityFoldsPass is false so the cite-check edge routes to plan-grade, where the fail-closed citeCheckFlag threads the blocking floor verdict to the correctness unit as --cite-check leads (the plan's own Group 1 test pins this shape). The comment is copied verbatim into shipped code and misstates behavior.

Phase 4's grade/SKILL.md section header says "Six regions" but enumerates seven edits (Edit 1 through Edit 7); each edit is individually anchored and complete, so the mislabeled count does not impair execution.

Phase 6's two new replay scripts diverge from the four sibling scripts' local style in the same directory: tab indentation, PEP8 one-per-line imports, and argparse subcommand CLI (plus a SCRIPT_DIR-default --out) versus the siblings' space indentation, compact comma-joined imports, module-level sys.argv execution, and cwd-relative output (baseline.py verified). The plan justifies the structural divergence (duplicating baseline.py's primitives because it executes its walk at import) but never names the stylistic one. Cosmetic and behavior-neutral: the whole thoughts/ tree is gitignored (verified via git check-ignore), so nothing shipped or lint-gated is affected, and consistent tabs are valid Python 3.

The Synthesis Notes defer whole-repo verification to 'the final Whole-Plan Verification block owned by validate', but no such section exists in the artifact — it ends at Phase 6 Notes/Deferred. Sibling plans (2026-09-01_13-01-59, 2026-08-31_16-41-15) carry a final ## Whole-Plan Verification section as the convention, so npm run check, npm test, the decision-codes guard, and the workflow-invariant check are left with no in-plan home a downstream stage can find.

A few REPLACE anchors quote the old text with a leading ellipsis (citations.ts Edits 1-2 and grade-panel.ts Edit 3 in Phase 1), so the implementer must locate the full region by grep on the quoted fragment rather than a byte-exact anchor; distinctive and locatable, but looser than the plan's usual exact-match discipline.

Acceptance a18's frozen evidence command targets packages/rpiv-pi/extensions/rpiv-core/subagent-usage.test.ts, but the plan's new token-stamping coverage lands in built-ins/verdict-outcome.test.ts (Phase 4); the command still exits 0 on the unchanged existing suite, yet the file-target divergence is acknowledged nowhere — unlike the explicit a2-a6 and a16 reconciliations the plan carries elsewhere.

Phase 1's new file built-ins/citations.test.ts opens with import { builtInWorkflows } from "./built-in-workflows.js" — from built-ins/ that specifier resolves to built-ins/built-in-workflows.js, which does not exist; the monolith exporting builtInWorkflows sits one directory up (extensions/rpiv-core/built-in-workflows.ts:1262), so the sibling specifier is only valid inside built-in-workflows.test.ts beside it, where the suites were probed. The block says "Create with exactly this content" and Phase 2's import merge does not correct it, so the copied-verbatim file fails module resolution and the phase's tsc/vitest AVs cannot pass as written; it also invents an import depth no built-ins/ file uses (verified: zero built-ins files reference the monolith).

Phase 1 emits two comments claiming the symbol check never touches the frontmatter, but the emitted code does not enforce that for Form B: the citedSymbols doc says Never reads the frontmatter and the read-block comment says the check runs never inside the frontmatter, yet for a citation inside the frontmatter (which the walk does resolve and read — Phase 2 itself pins frontmatter cites yielding claims with section frontmatter), Form A is incidentally empty via the proseStart clamp but Form B executes on body.slice(citeEnd, segEnd) — the remainder of the frontmatter line — with no proseStart guard, so a strict-shape token following a frontmatter cite is extracted and can emit a BLOCKING symbol finding; the false behavior claim ships verbatim in copied comment text

A few REPLACE specs quote only the tail of the old text with a leading ellipsis (Phase 1 citations.ts Edits 1-2 and grade-panel.ts Edits 3-4), so the implementer must locate the region by its named heading plus the quoted unique tail instead of a full old-text match — executable, mildly more search work.

a4's expect names a determinism-case half the suite never carries: no test exercises a FAILING floor verdict (e.g. a ghost cite) and asserts the claims sidecar still lands; the planCitationCheck code writes the sidecar unconditionally before return and the doc comment states every-round writes, so the behavior holds, but the frozen vitest command exits 0 without evidencing that half of the item's expect.

The new built-ins/verdict-outcome.ts imports ../subagent-usage.js, the first built-ins-to-parent-level module edge in the package (verified: no other built-ins file imports upward). The edge is DAG-clean (subagent-usage.ts imports only ./lane-usage.js, so no cycle) and effectively forced by grade-panel.ts consuming the factory, and the module stays in the off-entry-graph load pocket reached via register-built-in-workflows.ts's guarded dynamic import, so the documented peer-import constraint still holds — but the plan flags the barrel addition without calling out this new dependency-direction precedent.

Phase 5's built-in-workflows.test.ts edits do not compose with Phase 1's fail-closed citeCheckFlag. Phase 1 Group 3 inserts a plan-cite-check channel line into exactly the two confirm-describe tests that Phase 5 Edits 3-4 replace (grade panels never thread --prior; the degenerate all-passing fallback), so in the declared 1-before-5 apply order the REPLACE anchors cannot match the Phase-1-augmented text. Worse, the replacements plus all seven new --touched/--prior tests omit the plan-cite-check entry their named state needs, so loopOf plan-grade/plan-confirm units() and SHIP_DIMENSION_FANOUT.units() throw the halt preflight once Phase 1 lands (only the slice-gate test uses an uncited panel), and Phase 5's own vitest AV cannot pass as written; the order-independent proof holds because applying 5 before 1 instead breaks Phase 1 Group 3's anchored insertions against the retitled tests.
